title: Event registration service
context: Implement an in-memory event registration system: add events with a type, capacity and skill requirements, register and cancel participants, and list the events a participant is registered for. The doc comment lists the rules; the tests check them. This is modelled on the HackerRank task reported for GetYourGuide's backend interview (addEvent, registerParticipant, cancelRegistration, findRegisteredEvents). The reports don't say what requirements and skillLevel mean, so this version treats them as a minimum and an actual whole-number level.

points.title: Two maps: events and participants
points.why: One map from event id to the event gives direct lookup. A second map from participant id to event ids answers findRegisteredEvents without scanning every event.
points.fix: HashMap of event id to an Event (type, capacity, requirements, LinkedHashSet of participants) and HashMap of participant id to a LinkedHashSet of event ids. LinkedHashSet keeps registration order.

points.title: Check capacity, duplicates and skill before adding
points.why: Without these checks a full event takes another participant, a repeated participant is counted twice, and an unqualified one gets in.
points.fix: Return false when skillLevel < requirements, the event is full, or add() on the participant set returns false. Update the participant's event set only after the add succeeds.

points.title: Cancel updates both maps
points.why: If cancel only removes the participant from the event, findRegisteredEvents still lists the event and the two maps disagree.
points.fix: Remove from the event's participants; if that returned true, also remove the event id from the participant's set and return true.

points.title: Validate input and fail loudly
points.why: A typo in an event id should not look like an empty event, and a bad email should not be stored.
points.fix: One find helper that throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown events, plus an email check, before any map is changed.
